preamble: The voiced alveolar lateral fricative [ɮ] can lose its frication and become the lateral approximant [l]. A documented change in progress is found in Yami (Tao) of Orchid Island, Taiwan, where younger, Mandarin-dominant speakers increasingly replace traditional [ɮ] with [l]; Lai and Hsu (2013) link the rate of change to Mandarin competence, Mandarin-speaking frequency and weaker ties to the Yami community.

examples.note: Contact-induced change in progress: speakers with stronger Mandarin competence and weaker Yami social networks show the highest rate of [ɮ] > [l].

sources: Lai, L.-F., & Hsu, H. (2013). Contact-induced sound change: analysis of the alveolar lateral fricative in Yami. Journal of Estonian and Finno-Ugric Linguistics, 4(2), 31-50. https://doi.org/10.12697/jeful.2013.4.2.02
